rows.text: D’source’s documented lampshade starts with coloured cloth cut and joined into appliqué. A cardboard stencil marks repeated outlines; the matching pieces are cut in layers and bundled for later use.

The appliqués are machine-stitched onto cloth in plain and decorative patterns. Wooden or iron rings then give the shade its shape. This is one documented process, not a description of every Pipili workshop.
Prof. Bibhudutta Baral, Divyadarshan C. S. and Manasa K H, NID Bengaluru, “Traditional Applique Work — Making Process,” D’source. Lampshade sequence.
The documented lampshade uses repeated cloth pieces, machine stitching and supporting rings.
